A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same representation study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection, anomaly-detection, localization, feature-combination, and sensitivity experiments in Section 6 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds BRAVEn evaluations, detector comparisons, and a classifier-head experiment.

M1.justification: v2 adds BRAVEn audio/visual backbone options and a tested transformer classifier variant using a CLS-token prediction (Appendix E.3). These extend the evaluated architectures; the principal linear-probing, explanation, and anomaly-detection procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use FakeAVCeleb, AV-Deepfake1M, AVLips, DeepfakeEval-2024, and ExDDV for the same detection and explanation tasks. The added models and classifier experiments reuse existing downstream coverage; revised sample counts do not introduce a new dataset or scenario.

E2.justification: The detector comparison expands from AVFF and SpeechForensics to also evaluate AVAD, AuViRe, and RealForensics (v2 Table 3). Representation comparisons add BRAVEn audio and visual variants. Conversely, AVFF and SpeechForensics no longer participate in the reported AP comparison: their v1 Table 4 rows disappear from v2 Table 5.

E3.justification: Reported AV1M probing training/validation/test counts change from 45,000/5,000/10,000 to 22,972/2,527/5,133 (Section 5.1 and Appendix A). v2 also introduces the transformer-head control and Table 3's four-dataset and three-dataset averages, with differing baseline training regimes disclosed. The PDFs do not establish whether the count revisions reflect reruns or corrected reporting.

E4.justification: New Appendix E.3 and Table 8 systematically compare linear and transformer classifiers across ten feature types and the existing evaluation matrix, directly testing whether classifier capacity limits the conclusions. Figure 2 also extends localization analysis to BRAVEn. Earlier pooling, temporal-shift, layer-wise, spatial-explanation, and fusion analyses remain, despite relocation and renumbering.

E5.justification: Figure 4's uncertainty display and accompanying variance discussion remain unchanged. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence-interval procedures, or significance tests, and v2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: New results include BRAVEn, three detector baselines, and transformer heads. BRAVEn (V) obtains 84.6% mean OOD AUC in v2 Table 2; Table 8 reports FSFM at 40.9% with a linear head versus 72.3% with a transformer for AV1M-to-FAVC evaluation. Retained feature AUC/AP, anomaly, and pooling values are unchanged. Baseline AP results and several AVFF training/testing combinations are removed.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(3), their assumptions, and the mathematical scoring constructions remain equivalent. Neither version contains a theoretical proof or theorem that is added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: v1's abstract emphasizes that none of the features generalize reliably across datasets, and its conclusion identifies AV-HuBERT as strongest overall. v2 foregrounds state-of-the-art performance, specifically attributes superiority over complex approaches to BRAVEn's visual encoder, and concentrates the remaining generalization challenge on realistic in-the-wild data. This materially strengthens and refocuses the principal takeaway.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new classifier experiment as evidence that representations matter more than classifier complexity, while identifying the FSFM exception. Its explicit limitations paragraph further attributes real-world difficulty to diversity, missing modalities, and domain shifts. Most existing interpretations concerning shortcuts, semantic alignment, and complementarity are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-webpage pointer, BRAVEn checkpoint and preprocessing choices, and checkpoint/training-source information for the new detector baselines. Appendix E.3 specifies transformer width 768, four layers, eight attention heads, and projection operations. Appendix A also makes FAVC class filtering explicit, consistent with the restriction already stated in v1 Section 5.2.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for BRAVEn, RealForensics, AuViRe, and LRW, and broadens its positioning against evaluated detectors. The general related-work coverage and claim of systematically studying multiple representations remain intact; most citation changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: v2 revises the abstract and conclusion, compresses the contribution list into an inline findings summary, and streamlines model descriptions. It adds acknowledgments and a labeled limitations paragraph, and moves layer-wise analysis into Appendix E.2. The main section sequence and much of the methodological and results prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 reorganizes the principal result tables with modality columns, separates detector comparisons into Table 3, adds the paired classifier comparison in Table 8, and redraws Figure 2 with BRAVEn entries. Appendix plots are relocated. Figure 2 reverses classification/localization hatching while retaining the old caption description, introducing a caption–legend inconsistency.

improvement.justification: The expanded detector comparison and systematic classifier-capacity experiment strengthen support for the representation-focused conclusions beyond v1's narrower comparisons. These provide a modest net benefit, tempered by lost baseline AP coverage and Figure 2's new display inconsistency. The unexplained AV1M count revisions limit comparisons across versions, while the core methodology and most existing results remain unchanged.
